newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures rally after no rate hike.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures rally after no rate hike.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures rallied but ended off highs hit in fast-paced trade after the Federal Reserve left U.S. interest rates unchanged.
The U.S. discount rate remains at 5.00 percent, and the overnight Fed funds rate target still stands at 5.50 percent.

Stocks, which had lolled at softer levels, shot higher in tandem with a knee-jerk jump up in U.S. Treasury bond futures when the Fed's open market committee meeting ended without the rate increase that roughly half the market had expected.
"I think everybody is just shocked," said one Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 futures broker.
"We went up five handles without anything trading," he added. "It was all bid up."
"There were some serious players in here today," said another floor broker. "Fifty-lots were swinging around easily.... There were major-league buyers all day long."
He said price boards estimated volume in S&P 500 futures at about 77,000 contracts, with the bulk of that turnover occurring during the frenetic afternoon swings.
June S&P 500s briefly tracked T-bonds back to the minus side but drew renewed buying and powered back to even bigger gains and higher levels after bond futures closed soft.

Nearby S&P 500s futures climbed a second time and matched their all-time and contract high at 846.50 before edging off in trading that brokers said stayed fast-market for an hour after the Fed's decision was announced.
"It's still fast. I'm still trying to figure out what happened at 842.00," said another busy broker after June S&Ps had pulled back from 846.50.
Some said strength Tuesday in over-the-counter stocks buoyed the broader market and could support more gains soon.
"The thing that was impressive to me was the Nasdaq 100 and Composite held gains all day," said the first broker.
Brokers said the now-double top at 846.50 did not create a particularly worrisome technical formation, with one saying the contract could shimmy up to 848.80 or beyond soon.

Futures early on had dropped with T-bond futures and shrank the premium sufficiently to draw arbitrage sell programs. The pullback deepened enough that the Dow 30 average fell 50 points and triggered the New York Stock Exchange's curb on computer-assisted index arbitrage.
Fair value Tuesday was roughly 2.75 points premium. Arbitrage buy programs required about a 3.55-point premium. Sell programs need about a premium of 1.95 points or less.

At settlement, June S&P 500s had climbed 8.50 points to 844.55, Value Lines rose 4.60 to 740.80, Nikkei 225 fell 220.0 points to 20,355.0, Midcap 400s rose 2.40 to 272.30, NYSE Composite rose 4.20 to 439.90, Russell added 2.50 to 371.50, and Nasdaq 100 futures soared 29.35 points to 946.25.
